comparisons.peer_summary: At December 31, 2024, the notional amounts of SBLCs classified as investment grade and non-investment grade were $25.0 billion and $10.1 billion, while consumer SBLCs amounted to $1.0 billion.
comparisons.comparison: Both C and BAC disclose credit quality metrics for financial instruments that include specific exposures to consumer-related or Wealth-managed segments, categorized by investment vs. non-investment grade. C discloses that $25.9 billion of Private Bank loans (a Wealth segment) lack FICO scores and are rated by internal risk ratings, with 83% rated investment grade. Similarly, BAC discloses that its Standby Letter of Credit (SBLC) portfolio, which includes $1.0 billion of consumer SBLCs, was classified as $25.0 billion investment grade and $10.1 billion non-investment grade based on the credit quality of the underlying reference name. While C focuses on unsecured/wealth loans evaluated via internal ratings due to missing FICO scores, BAC applies similar investment/non-investment grading to SBLCs including consumer exposure, utilizing internal categorizations for risk management.

comparisons.peer_summary: The firm assigns regulatory risk ratings to loans based on U.S. federal bank regulatory agency definitions, with 93% of total loans rated pass/non-criticized as of December 2024 and 92% as of December 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Both C and GS disclose the percentage of their loan portfolios that meet high credit quality standards (investment grade/pass) as of year-end, highlighting strong portfolio health. C reports that 83% of its Private Bank loans (which lack FICO scores) were rated investment grade as of Dec 31, 2024. GS reports that 93% of its total loans were rated pass/non-criticized (the highest regulatory rating) as of Dec 31, 2024. While C restricts this metric to a specific Wealth segment and GS applies it to the total loan book, both highlight the proportion of loans deemed low-risk by their respective internal or regulatory rating systems.

comparisons.comparison: Both C and MS disclose that internal risk ratings are the primary basis for determining credit quality (investment vs. non-investment grade) for specific loan types where external scores may not be fully utilized or are supplemented. C states that Private Bank loans without FICO scores are "primarily evaluated for credit risk based on their internal risk ratings." MS states that "Investment grade/non-investment grade determination is based on the internal credit rating of the reference obligation" and that these internal ratings serve as the assessment of credit risk. Both firms rely on internal models/ratings to categorize credit quality for segments that may not rely solely on standard external credit scores.
